a freeze-and-thew cycle induces proteolysis of the microtuble-associated protein Tau in rodent brain homogenates, and the proteolysis is more pronounced when the extracts are kept at −20 °C than −80 °C.

freeze-and-thaw of brain homogenates can induce proteolytic events on Tau, resulting in the production of an ~25 kDa Tau species, which is detected in Western blots using anti-Tau antibodies and can lead to overestimation of Tau levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the freeze-and-thaw procedure can lead to proteolytic events in Tau, and that this phenomenon can be avoided by using fresh samples.
freeze-and-thaw cycles should not be employed to prepare samples for WB analysis of total and phosphorylated forms of Tau.
freeze-and-thaw cycles should be avoided in the preparation of brain extracts for the biochemical assessment in Tau-related neurotoxicity in rodents.
